key_insight: System 1 models made rapid, probability-based decisions, performing best on medical knowledge and text understanding and less reliably on clinical judgement and imaging.
clinical_relevance: These models may support narrowly defined clinical workflows, but weaker judgement and imaging performance warrant clinician oversight and task-specific validation.
method: Evaluated four models zero-shot on 86 public tasks across 14 clinical domains and 20 languages.
Grouped tasks into six capability tiers; assessed AUROC, calibration and language effects.
Compared performance with published results and generative models, and measured local inference time and energy.
evidence_signal: Across 179,111 cases, mean AUROC for the best model per task ranged from 0.94 for medical knowledge to 0.69 for volumetric findings; imaging averaged 0.09 below text.
watch_item: Performance depended strongly on language: accuracy on identical questions fell by up to 39 percentage points from English to Yoruba.
paper_title: The Value of System 1 Models in Medicine
